summary: Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar and serves as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Antonio Vigilante specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning his doctorate at the University of Bari, he taught at Liceo Enea Silvio Piccolomini and held a teaching post at the University of Siena (2025–2026).
Antonín Jan Jungmann (1775–1854) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Charles University (Dr.med. 1800–1805) and served there as Professor of Medicine from 1808 to 1850.

Anuj Misra works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Cape Town and the University of Canterbury under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker, later holding posts at MPIWG, Free University of Berlin, and the University of Copenhagen.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee (1911–1999) was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Calcutta, where he later taught Pali, and served as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Anupam Chakraborty is associated with Indology. He earned a BBA from Bengal School of Technology and Management and studied for an MBA at the Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur (2023–2025).
Anuradha Seneviratna (1938–2009) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Peradeniya (c. 1961–1965) and later served there as a professor from circa 1984 to 2004.

Anushka Kahandagamage specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed degrees at the University of Colombo, South Asian University, and the University of Otago (PhD 2021–2024), and held a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard University (2025–2026).

Anvita Abbi (born 1949) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She studied at Cornell University (c. 1971–1975) and served on the editorial board at Jawaharlal Nehru University from circa 1976 to 2013.
Aparajita Kundu is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She earned her PhD at Jadavpur University and serves as an Assistant Professor at Surendranath College.

Aram Frenkian (1898–1964) worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University and the University of Bucharest, and under Antoine Meillet, Louis Finot, and Émile Bréhier, later serving as Professor of Greek at Chernivtsi and Bucharest.

Archibald Campbell (1805–1874) was an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Glasgow, Edinburgh (Dr.med.), and Cambridge, where he later served as Lecturer in Indian Law at the University of Cambridge and Pembroke College.

Archibald Campbell Carlleyle (1831–1897) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a curator at the Riddell Museum and as an assistant to Alexander Cunningham at the Archaeological Survey of India (1871–1885).

Archibald Edward Gough (1845–1915) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Lincoln College, Oxford, under Monier Monier-Williams. He held professorships at Benares Sanskrit College, Presidency University, and served as Principal at Aliah University and the University of Allahabad.

Archie John Bahm (1907–1996) specialized in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Albion College and the University of Michigan, and held faculty posts at Texas Tech, University of Denver, and the University of New Mexico.

Arend Willem Mauritz Odé (1887–1951) was a linguist who earned his PhD from Leiden University, studying under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck and Holger Pedersen. He later taught and served as conrector at Grotius College.
Arghyadip Mondal is a scholar in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and Indology, attested as a PhD researcher at Ghent University in 2026.

Ariana Maki is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Ohio State University and held posts at the University of Idaho, University of Colorado Boulder, and the University of Virginia.
Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein and succeeded Marcelle Lalou, holding an attested post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 1972.
Arild Engelsen Ruud works in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the London School of Economics (1991–1995) and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 2007.
